publicComment.summary: Fill out a Public Comment form and hand it to the Town Secretary before the 6 p.m. meeting starts (there is a marked tray near the Town Secretary's seat in Jody Smith Hall, the council chambers at Town Hall), and you get up to 3 minutes to speak near the start of the meeting, on any topic. For public hearing items you speak when the Mayor opens that hearing. Work sessions have the same comment slot.
publicComment.howToRegister: Download the Public Comment form (flowermound.gov/documentcenter/view/10425) or pick one up at Town Hall, fill in your name, address and the agenda item or subject, mark support or opposition, and give it to the Town Secretary before the meeting is scheduled to begin (forms are accepted until the public comment portion ends). State your name and town when you start, direct remarks to the Town Council, and keep to 3 minutes; other speakers can donate time on posted agenda items only, up to 9 minutes total. Anyone using slides or video must give the digital file to the Town Secretary's Office by 12 noon on the meeting day.
publicComment.deadline: Before the meeting is scheduled to begin (forms accepted until the public comment portion concludes); electronic presentation files by 12 noon on meeting day
publicComment.writtenCommentMethod: Email the Mayor and full council at once at towncouncil@flowermound.gov (listed on the Town Council page); emails are public records. No online eComment form is offered.
publicComment.notes: The Mayor may adjust time limits. The form is a public record and your name and municipality appear in the official minutes. Council can only respond to non-agenda topics with a statement of fact, existing policy, or a proposal to put the subject on a future agenda. No remote or virtual speaking option is described on the Town's pages.

youthPrograms.name: Flower Mound Youth Action Council
youthPrograms.ages: Flower Mound residents ages 14 to 19 in grades 9 to 12 (Flower Mound High, Marcus High, private or homeschool)
youthPrograms.description: Up to 22 students serve one-year terms as an advisory group to the Town Council, Parks Board, Executive Team and Parks & Recreation on issues affecting youth, through problem solving, education, social activities and service projects; selection is based on leadership, community involvement and vision.
youthPrograms.applyWindow: Not stated on the program page; apply through the online Form Center application (contact Kimberly Cheek, kimberly.cheek@flowermound.gov, 972-874-6300, or the program line 972-874-6276)

youthPrograms.name: Lewisville/Flower Mound Teen Court
youthPrograms.ages: Teens cited for a Class C misdemeanor in town limits; volunteers must be middle or high school students ages 13 to 18 who attend school or live in the greater Lewisville area
youthPrograms.description: Voluntary alternative to paying a fine: after pleading guilty or no contest in Municipal Court and paying a $20 fee, the teen is sentenced by a jury of peers to community service and jury duty, and the case is dismissed on completion. Court alternates between Lewisville and Flower Mound, generally on 1st and 3rd Tuesdays; fall 2026 Flower Mound dates are Sept. 22, Oct. 20, Nov. 17 and Dec. 15 (Lewisville: Sept. 8, Oct. 6, Nov. 3, Dec. 1). Contact teencourt@cityoflewisville.com or 972-219-3799.
youthPrograms.applyWindow: Rolling; volunteers observe a session first, then sign a volunteer agreement (sign-ups at volunteer.cityoflewisville.com)
